verses.1: Shaul spoke to Jonathan, his son, and to all his servants, telling them to kill David. Jonathan, son of Shaul, desired David very much.
verses.2: And Jonathan told David, “Shaul, my father, is asking for your death. Now, please stay in the room tonight. You will be put in a prison cell.”
verses.3: And I went and stood by my father’s side in the field where you were also there. I spoke to him, and I told him what I had seen.
verses.4: And Jonathan spoke well of David to his father Saul. He said to him, “Do not sin against King David. For he did not sin against you at all. Instead, his actions were good for you.”
verses.5: And he put his soul into his arms, and he wrapped the Philistine in it. Then Jehovah performed a great miracle for all Israel. You saw this, and you were rejoiced. But why do you sin against innocent blood, in order to kill David?
verses.6: Shaul heard the voice of Yehonatan. Shaul praised the name of Jehovah. May He live forever!
verses.7: And Johanan called for David. He told him all these things. Then Johanan brought David before Shaul. He stood before him as if he were a king.
verses.8: And the war continued. David went out and fought against the Philistines. He defeated them greatly, and they were driven away from him.
verses.9: And the spirit of Jehovah was evil upon Shaul. He sat in his house, with his harp in his hand. David played music at that time.
verses.10: Shaul tried to break the ship into pieces by using Dovid and the wall. But they were able to stop him. Then, Shaul tried to break the ship through the wall. Dovid performed a miracle and managed to lift the ship up during the night.
verses.11: And Shaul sent servants to David’s house, so that they could guard it and kill him in the morning. Michal, David’s wife, reported this to him, saying, “If you don’t protect your life tonight, you will die tomorrow.”
verses.12: And David went down from the palace, along with the ark. He ran away and fled.
verses.13: And she took the ointments from the jar, poured them onto the altar. Then she put on her most beautiful clothes, and covered herself with them.
verses.14: And Shaul sent demons to take away David. And they said, “He is sick.”
verses.15: And Sheol sent the devils to see David, saying, “Bring him before me so that I may kill him.”
verses.16: And the devils came in. And behold, those who were terrifying and mighty from their very nature stood before them.
verses.17: And Shaul said to Michal, “Why do you deceive me in this way? You sent your enemy to kill me.” Then Michal said to Shaul, “He told me to send for him, so that he could kill me.”
verses.18: And David ran away, and he went to Mount Sinai. There, he told Samuel everything that Saul had done to him. Then they went together, and they sat down in the valleys.
verses.19: And he told Shaul, “Look, David’s sons are in Babylon.”
verses.20: And Shaul sent demons to take away David. He saw that the prophets were coming forward. Samuel stood among them. A divine spirit covered Shaul’s demons, and they also came forward.
verses.21: And they reported to Shaul. He then sent other servants. They also brought those people with them. Shaul gathered all those people together, and he sent thirty servants to deal with them.
verses.22: And he also went up to the high mountain. There, he asked, “Where are Samuel and David?” And they replied, “They are in the heavens.”
verses.23: And he went there to the heights of Nayot. There, a divine spirit rested upon him. He continued to walk along, until he reached the heights of Nayot.
verses.24: And he also stripped off his clothes. He was brought before Shemael. All that day and all that night, he remained in that state. Then Shaul said among the prophets, “Alas!”
